named_events.loss_description: net claims for Hurricanes Harvey, Irma and Maria being booked at $215 million. Hurricane losses in this the most expensive year for natural losses ever, hit the reinsurance and property insurances classes most heavily with the majority of losses being borne by the 2017 year of account. The 2017 account will pick up almost all of the reinsurance loss from the 2017 hurricanes together with a share of direct property loss.
Hurricane Harvey which caused extensive flooding in Houston was the most significant event for the division.
The $140 billion of catastrophe losses across the sector led to capital destruction and reserve deficits, and as a result the market is turning.

data.standardized_narrative: Syndicate 33 reported a gross prior year development release of GBP 264.369 million, representing a 17.47% release of its opening gross claims outstanding. This favorable development was primarily driven by releases from catastrophes in prior years, supported by good gross underwriting and fees earned from third parties. The reinsurance account, particularly property catastrophe-focused business, experienced benign loss activity in 2015 and 2016, contributing to these releases. The claims development triangle is distorted by a large Reinsurance to Close transaction and was not used for this calculation.

data.data_quality_notes: The claims development triangle is distorted by a large Reinsurance to Close (RITC) transaction, making it unreliable for calculating prior year development. The prior year development figure is taken from the 'Over-provision in respect of prior claims and claim adjustment expenses' line in Note 10, which is a direct statement of the movement.
